f.t: New research highlights need for surgeon peer support as RCS England launches SUPPORT2
f.x: More than 88% of surgeons surveyed say surgeon-specific peer support is needed, as RCS England launches SUPPORT2 with 16 new and five returning site teams. The Royal College of Surgeons of England (RCS England) recently launched SUPPORT2, the next phase of its surgeon peer-support improvement programme.

f.t: Outcomes of concomitant lacertus release and carpal tunnel release in patients with double crush syndrome: a cohort study
f.x: Concomitant lacertus and carpal tunnel release improved symptoms in 51 patients with clinical double crush syndrome. Return-to-work duration was five weeks, and 73% of the patients were satisfied three months after treatment.
f.s: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

f.t: Histopathological Predictors of Extranodal Extension in Oral Cavity Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Five-Year Retrospective Cohort Study
f.x: Extranodal extension (ENE) of cervical nodal metastases is a major adverse prognostic feature in oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCSCC). Despite this clinical significance, the primary tumour histopathological features that independently predict ENE as distinct from nodal metastasis remain poorly characterised.
f.s: British Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
